analysis.investment_thesis: Unified Data-Tech is a tiny Rs 619 Cr Mumbai IT services shop with a broken story — ROE of 0.36% at a P/E of 21 is a value trap, not a GARP opportunity. Without visible growth or margin data to compute a PEG, there's no case to buy.
key_strengths: IT services sector has sector tailwinds from digital spend
Small-cap size (Rs 619 Cr) leaves room to compound if execution turns
key_risks: ROE of 0.36% is effectively zero — capital isn't earning anything
P/E of 21 is unjustified given near-zero profitability; PEG likely far above 1.5
Negligible institutional interest (FII 0.57%, DII 5.89%) signals lack of conviction/liquidity
red_flags: ROE near zero despite 21x P/E multiple
No visible growth rate to anchor PEG calculation
Undifferentiated 'customized IT solutions' positioning in a crowded sector
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Every stock needs a story, and I can't find one here. A 0.36% ROE means the business is generating essentially nothing on its equity base — yet the market is pricing it at 21x earnings. For a fast-grower thesis to work I'd need 20%+ revenue growth and a PEG under 1.0; for a stalwart thesis I'd need durable 15%+ ROE. This stock qualifies as neither. The IT Enabled Services label is generic — Mumbai is full of small IT shops offering "innovative and customized solutions," which is code for no moat.

Promoter holding at 60% is the one encouraging data point, but insider ownership alone doesn't pay the bills. With FII at 0.57% and DII at under 6%, smart money has passed. I'd want to see two to three years of topline acceleration, margin expansion, and ROE climbing toward 15%+ before this becomes interesting. Until then, pass — there are better small-caps with real earnings growth at similar multiples.
